booklet.title: Upgrading to kajenn 0.10.0: login with the _auth application, and what each application must change
booklet.author: Giovanni Porcari

purpose.p: kajenn 0.10.0 moves authentication out of _server into one application with code _auth. This booklet is for the developers of the applications that run on kajenn. It states what changed, how to set up login, a generic checklist, and the changes each known application needs.

Every fact carries its source. A source without a repository prefix is a path in the kajenn repository at tag v0.10.0. A source with a prefix (kajenn-webrtc/, sourcerer_v2/, genropy-kajenn/, hetzner-kube/) is a path in that repository, read on 2026-11-17.

list.item: kajenn 0.10.0 (tag v0.10.0, on PyPI).
A storage_key on the server: the _auth records are written encrypted.
For OIDC login: external_url on the server.

step.title: What changed

list.item: Authentication belongs to the application with code _auth, class AuthApplicationBase. A server without it authenticates nobody.
_server has no login, no users and no tokens.
One store, AuthStore, with the file backend FileAuthStore. It holds users, groups, tag records, tokens and login failure counters.
A user record has status (waiting, confirmed, banned), groups, primary_group and system. Only confirmed authenticates.
A token belongs to a user. It carries "*" or a list of the user's tags.
A tag must have a tag record. An application declares its tags in declared_tags and its program users in system_users. Other tags are created with /_auth/tags/create_tag.
The management of users, groups, tags and tokens asks AUTH_ADMIN. The _server sections ask SERVER_ADMIN. SUPERADMIN is removed.
The session keeps the identity and the group of an avatar. The tags are asked to /_auth/avatar at every request.
avatar.data lasts one request. Data for the whole session goes in session.data.
external_url is optional. It switches on the capability external_links. The OIDC routes require it.
Data under site:users and site:api_keys is not read. At the first start the server log carries the password of _temporary_admin.
Session dumps and snapshots of earlier versions cannot be loaded. Delete them before the first start.

step.fact: A server that does not mount _auth authenticates nobody: a presented Authorization header answers 401 and a session gives no identity.
AuthApplicationBase has code and mount equal to AUTHENTICATION_CODE, which is "_auth" (src/kajenn/auth/mixin.py:71).
The _server routes login, logout, login_methods, users/..., tokens/... and auth/... are removed.
AuthCore, UserStore, FileUserStore, ApiKeyStore and FileApiKeyStore are removed. AuthStore and FileAuthStore import from kajenn.
The store holds five kinds of record: user, group, tag, token, login failure counter.
The user record has status in place of enabled, and the fields groups, primary_group, system, email, external_ids. Only confirmed authenticates.
A token belongs to a user and carries "*" or a non-empty list of tags, a subset of the user's tags. label is removed.
The management refuses a tag that has no tag record. The tags an application uses are declared in declared_tags, or created with /_auth/tags/create_tag.
SUPERADMIN is removed. Users, groups, tags and tokens ask AUTH_ADMIN; the _server sections, tasks included, ask SERVER_ADMIN.
The session stores the identity and the group of an avatar, never its tags. At every request the server asks /_auth/avatar for the tags. A refused identity loses its session.
avatar.data lives for one request. Data that must last for the session is written in session.data.
The capability external_links is true when the server has an external_url.
OidcMethod declares env_requires = "external_links" on its start and callback routes.
FileAuthStore reads only site:auth. Records under site:users and site:api_keys are ignored. The server log carries the password of _temporary_admin.
A session dump or snapshot of an earlier version cannot be loaded. Whoever upgrades deletes the session dump and the snapshot file before the first start.

section.title: Mount _auth in the recipe
section.p: The recipe writes one application element with code _auth. The words under it configure the store, the lockout, the OIDC providers and the self registration.

example.title: Recipe from docs/guides/authentication.md
example.code:
from genro_bag.resolvers import EnvResolver from kajenn import AuthApplicationBase, FileAuthStore
def applications_section(self, cfg): """The authentication application: who keeps the users, the lockout, the external provider.""" apps = cfg.applications() auth_app = apps.application(code="_auth", app_class=AuthApplicationBase, cache_ttl=60) auth_app.store(store_class=FileAuthStore, mount="site", prefix="auth") auth_app.login(max_attempts=3, backoff=10) auth_app.oidc().provider( code="google", issuer="https://accounts.example.com", client_id="client-123", client_secret=EnvResolver("GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"), ) auth_app.self_registration(status="waiting", tags=["shop_guest"])

list.item: cache_ttl: seconds an answer of _auth stays cached. Default 300.
store(store_class, ...): without the word the store is FileAuthStore on site:auth.
login(max_attempts, backoff): defaults 5 attempts, 30 seconds.
oidc().provider(code, issuer, client_id, client_secret, scopes): one per provider. scopes defaults to openid email profile.
self_registration(status, tags): what happens to a provider user the store does not have.

section.fact: The recipe above is the documented form of the _auth element.
The _auth grammar has the words store, login, oidc, provider (code, issuer, client_id, client_secret, scopes) and self_registration (status, tags).
cache_ttl defaults to 300; the store defaults to FileAuthStore on site:auth; the lockout defaults to 5 attempts and 30 seconds.

section.title: The first administrator
section.p: An empty store has no administrator. At startup _auth writes _temporary_admin and logs its password. Enter with it and create a real user with AUTH_ADMIN (and SERVER_ADMIN for the _server sections). _temporary_admin is then deleted.
section.fact: The log line is application %s: temporary administrator %s, password %s, at level warning.
When a user other than _temporary_admin holds AUTH_ADMIN, _auth deletes _temporary_admin. A restart while it still exists writes it again with a new password.

section.title: Password login

list.item: POST /_auth/login with {identity, password, group}. group is optional.
A refusal answers status 200 with {"error": ...}. Check the body.
An Authorization: Basic header is checked on the same users.

section.fact: /_auth/login answers {session_id, identity, group, tags, groups}, or 200 with {"error": ...}.

section.title: Replace a static bearer with a token of a system user
section.p: A fixed bearer of the recipe no longer exists. Declare a system user in the application. An administrator issues it a gak_ token.

example.title: Declared tags and system user, from docs/guides/authentication.md

section.p: The answer carries the key once. The client sends it as Authorization: Bearer gak_....
section.fact: A fixed bearer becomes a gak_ token of a system user.
At startup _auth writes the declared tags and system users that do not exist. A system user gets system true and no token.
/_auth/tokens/issue takes {user, tags, expires_at}; the key is returned only once.

section.title: OIDC login

list.item: The provider goes under the _auth element: auth_app.oidc().provider(code, issuer, client_id, client_secret).
Write client_secret as a resolver, for example EnvResolver("...").
The server needs external_url. The default template reads KAJENN_EXTERNAL_URL.
Register <external_url>/_auth/oidc:<code>/callback as redirect URI with the provider.
The login starts at /_auth/oidc:<code>/start?next=....

section.p: How a provider user is found in the store:

list.item: The user whose external_ids holds the token's iss + sub.
Else, with email and email_verified true, the one user with that email. {iss, sub} is added to its external_ids.
Else self_registration: absent, the login is refused; present, a user is written with identity = the verified email.

section.p: The provider attributes tags and identity_claim are removed. The tags of a provider user come from its store record.
section.fact: The OIDC routes move from /_server/auth/oidc:<code>/... to /_auth/oidc:<code>/.... The redirect_uri becomes <external_url>/_auth/oidc:<code>/callback.
_server_app.oidc().provider(...) becomes auth_app.oidc().provider(...). The provider attributes tags and identity_claim are removed.
link_user looks up iss + sub, then the one user with the verified email, then calls register_user.
The default template writes cfg.server(external_url=EnvResolver("KAJENN_EXTERNAL_URL", default="")).
login_methods lists only the methods whose required capability is on: without external_url the OIDC providers are left out.

section.title: Replace a custom credential check
section.p: Subclass AuthApplicationBase. Override verify_credential(credential). Mount the subclass with code _auth. The answer is {identity, group, tags, data, valid_until}, or HTTPUnauthorized.
A login method of a subclass is registered with register_auth_method on the AuthApplicationBase subclass.
section.fact: verify_credential(credential) receives the Authorization value and answers {identity, group, tags, data, valid_until}. It accepts Basic and Bearer gak_....
The route /_auth/authenticate receives channel and calls self.verify_credential(credential): the channel does not reach verify_credential.
register_auth_method(method) is a member of AuthApplicationBase.
The guide has a full SiteAuth example that overrides verify_credential.

step.title: Upgrade checklist

row.cell: cfg.authentication() with users, tokens, credentials, basic_user, bearer_token, jwt, cache_ttl
auth_app.store(store_class=...); cache_ttl as attribute of the _auth element
Removed. Custom check: subclass with verify_credential
gak_ token of a system user (/_auth/tokens/issue)
Removed. A JWT issued elsewhere: verify_credential in a subclass
Removed. Tags from the store record

cell.c: from kajenn.server_app import AuthMethod, PasswordMethod, OidcMethod, safe_next_path

row.cell: AuthCore, UserStore, ApiKeyStore and their file classes
Same names on a subclass of AuthApplicationBase
Any tag written in a rule
Users in site:users, keys in site:api_keys
Not read. Create them again with _temporary_admin

step.fact: The recipe elements authentication and channels are removed. A recipe that still writes them fails with the error of the grammar.
AsgiServer(..., credential_cache_ttl=5) raises TypeError.
The server members auth_core, user_store, api_key_store, channels and authentication_route(channel) are removed.
ServerApplication loses login_policy, oidc_providers, auth_section, register_auth_method and read_declared_login_surface. That code moves to a subclass of AuthApplicationBase.
AuthMethod, PasswordMethod, OidcMethod and safe_next_path are removed from kajenn.server_app. OidcMethod.get_safe_next_path replaces safe_next_path.
A custom authentication answer adds group.

section.title: meetlot (kajenn-webrtc)

list.item: pyproject.toml pins kajenn>=0.9.2,<0.10. Raise it.
site.py: the static bearer_token of identity webrtc, tag rooms, becomes a gak_ token of a system user.
site.py: the provider keycloak moves from the _server element to the _auth element. identity_claim='sub' is removed. external_url stays.
auth.py: the imports from kajenn.server_app move to kajenn.auth_app. safe_next_path becomes OidcMethod.get_safe_next_path.
auth.py: MeetlotServer(ServerApplication).register_auth_method moves to a subclass of AuthApplicationBase.
auth.py: KeycloakMethod.callback attaches Avatar(subject, tags). In 0.10.0 the session identity must be a user of the _auth store.
auth.py: avatar_from_claims writes expires_at, name, email in avatar.data. require() and Account.me read them on later requests. In 0.10.0 they are gone after the login request.
auth.py: the tags meetlot_host and meetlot_admin come from the Keycloak groups. How groups become tags is an open decision (see the decisions).
The path /_server/auth/oidc:keycloak/... becomes /_auth/oidc:keycloak/... in auth.py, welcome.html and tests/test_auth.py. application.py and pages/call.py use it through LOGIN.
Tags to declare: meetlot_host, meetlot_admin, rooms.
Keycloak (realm softwell, client meetlot): the redirect URI becomes https://meetlot.genro.com/_auth/oidc:keycloak/callback, in deploy/keycloak-meetlot.json and in Keycloak.
Point to check: deploy/meetlot.yaml has readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mounts only /tmp. FileAuthStore writes records and needs writable persistent storage.

section.fact: The dependency is "kajenn>=0.9.2,<0.10".
cfg.authentication().credentials().bearer_token(identity="webrtc", token=EnvResolver(ACCESS_CODE_VARIABLE), tags=ROOMS_TAG); ROOMS_TAG is "rooms" (kajenn-webrtc/src/kajenn_webrtc/access.py:14).
apps.application(code='_server', app_class=MeetlotServer) with server.oidc().provider(code='keycloak', ..., scopes='openid email profile groups', identity_claim='sub').
cfg.server(external_url=self.public_url).
Imports ServerApplication from kajenn.server_app, safe_next_path from kajenn.server_app.auth_method, OidcMethod from kajenn.server_app.oidc_method.
LOGIN = '/_server/auth/oidc:keycloak/start?next=/call'.
require() refuses when identity.data.get('expires_at', 0) <= time.time().
avatar_from_claims gives meetlot_host to every user and meetlot_admin to members of KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_GROUP; it builds Avatar(subject, tags) and writes expires_at, name, email in avatar.data.
KeycloakMethod.callback calls session.attach_avatar(avatar_from_claims(claims)) and redirects to safe_next_path(target).
A handler that attaches an Avatar to a session attaches an identity of the _auth store.
MeetlotServer(ServerApplication) overrides register_auth_method to replace the keycloak method with KeycloakMethod.
Account.me reads identity.data.get('name', ...).
Two links point to /_server/auth/oidc:keycloak/start?next=/call (lines 3 and 4).
The tests call /_server/auth/oidc:keycloak/start and /callback (lines 160, 165, 173).
application.py imports LOGIN and redirects to it (lines 62, 68). pages/call.py:18 imports it too.
"redirectUris": ["https://meetlot.genro.com/_server/auth/oidc:keycloak/callback"].
KEYCLOAK_ISSUER is https://auth.gpkube.genro.dev/realms/softwell; KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID is meetlot (line 56).
The container has readOnlyRootFilesystem: true; the only volume mount is /tmp, an emptyDir (lines 68, 73).

section.title: sourcerer v2

list.item: It pins kajenn==0.5.0.
Its Keycloak login goes through genropy gnrauth:oidc, not kajenn. No Keycloak change.

config.py writes cfg.channels() with authentication_route="/api/auth/authenticate". The element is removed. The logic of AuthTools.authenticate moves to a subclass of AuthApplicationBase mounted as _auth, and the answer adds group.
AuthTools.authenticate branches on channel (telegram). verify_credential receives no channel.
Other breaks between 0.5 and 0.10 are not about authentication: McpOpenApiApplication is removed in 0.9.0; the channel rest is renamed api in 0.9.0. See the 0.9.x sections of CHANGELOG.md.

section.p: The statement on genropy gnrauth:oidc comes from the survey of 2026-11-17; this booklet carries no source line for it.
section.fact: kajenn==0.5.0.
Started as gnrkajenn sourcerer --config src/sourcerer_core/tools/config.py.
cfg.channels() with channel(name=name, authentication_route=AUTHENTICATION_ROUTE) for rest, mcp, telegram; AUTHENTICATION_ROUTE = "/api/auth/authenticate" (line 41).
AuthTools.authenticate(credential, channel) answers {identity, tags, data}, without group; for the telegram channel it calls telegram_avatar (line 84).
from kajenn.applications.mcp import McpOpenApiApplication.
In 0.9.0 McpOpenApiApplication is removed and the channel rest is renamed api.

section.title: sourcerer v1
section.p: It does not use kajenn. No change.

section.title: kajenn-orchestra
section.p: PR #44 (Prometheus families of the SPA pool) is merged in develop on 2026-11-17. It raises the dependency to kajenn>=0.10.0. Its tests mount AuthApplicationBase and read GET /_server/metrics with a gak_ token of a user of _auth. The latest release is still 0.7.0.
section.fact: State MERGED at 2026-11-17T15:28:49Z, base develop.
pyproject.toml changes kajenn>=0.9.0 to kajenn>=0.10.0; tests/orchestration/test_orchestration_prometheus_metrics.py reads /_server/metrics with a token of _auth.
The latest release is v0.7.0 (2026-11-13).

section.title: genropy-kajenn
section.p: GnrAppWrapper.authenticate is used as authentication_route. Its answer has no group. How genropy-kajenn authenticates after 0.10.0 is an open decision of the owner (see the decisions).
section.fact: authenticate(credential, channel) verifies a Bearer on adm.api_token and answers {identity, tags, data, valid_until} (line 123).
The dependency is "kajenn>=0.9.0".

step.title: Open decisions and known issues
step.p: The open decisions are listed at the end of this booklet. They have no proposal yet. The known issue is listed under limits.

limits.limit: A WSX connection keeps the avatar of its handshake.

decision.question: How do the groups of an OIDC provider become tags of a user: in kajenn through a recipe rule, or in the application through a subclass? meetlot depends on it.
How does genropy-kajenn authenticate its adm.api_token credentials after 0.10.0?
